summary: Implemented 1v1 Quick Play on mobile: added useMatchmakingQueue hook (queue state machine with join/poll/cancel/cleanup) and QuickPlayCard + SearchingOverlay on HomeScreen. The hook POSTs to /api/duel/queue to join, polls GET every ~2s, handles matched/waiting/expired/409/error states, and DELETEs on cancel or unmount. On match, navigates to /duel/:id which drops into the existing DuelRoomScreen. No backend changes needed.
goal: Add 1v1 Quick Play to mobile app -- port web matchmaking queue UI to HomeScreen using existing /api/duel/queue backend

learnings.insight: The mobile typecheck runs via the mobile/tsconfig.json (separate from the main app tsconfig). The main app typecheck covers everything including mobile via the @app alias. Both pass clean.
learnings.action: Run both `pnpm typecheck` (from app/) and `cd app/mobile && npx tsc --noEmit` to verify mobile-specific types.

learnings.insight: No new test files were created because the verifier owns tests. The hook useMatchmakingQueue is testable in isolation -- it manages state + intervals + fetch calls. The SearchingOverlay is a pure presentational component.
learnings.action: Tests should cover: join flow (waiting -> polling -> matched navigation), 409 resume polling, timeout on expired, error display, cancel with DELETE, and interval cleanup on unmount.

learnings.insight: Quick Play uses the same apiFetch (Bearer token) and the same /api/duel/queue endpoints as the web. No new auth paths or trust boundaries. Category is hardcoded to 'tech' (not user-derived). No paid features ported.
learnings.action: Verify the hook does not introduce any new trust boundaries or bypass existing auth patterns.

learnings.insight: The SearchingOverlay has role=dialog with aria-modal=true and an assertive live region for screen reader announcements. All buttons meet 48px minimum height. The overlay prevents interaction with the home screen behind it.
learnings.action: Test keyboard/screen-reader accessibility of the overlay states (searching, timeout, error).

learnings.insight: 2 files changed/created, 0 new dependencies, all 3 quality gates pass (lint, typecheck, 681 tests).
